hints: Focus on what functional groups in santonin can react, look for the ester, the ketone and the carbon-carbon double bonds.
Warm dilute acid hydrolyses the cyclic ester to give one $\text{-COOH}$ group and one $\text{-OH}$ group, count how many $\text{O-H}$ protons that creates.
Cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$ adds two $\text{-OH}$ groups across each $\text{C=C}$ without cleavage, then add all $\text{-OH}$ and $\text{-COOH}$ protons that react with Na.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reactive functional groups**

Santonin contains three key types. A cyclic ester (a lactone), a ketone $\text{C=O}$, and two $\text{C=C}$ double bonds in the left six-membered ring.

Remember: Na metal reacts with $\text{O-H}$ protons in alcohols and carboxylic acids:
$$\text{2ROH + 2Na} \rightarrow \text{2RONa + H}_2$$
$$\text{2RCOOH + 2Na} \rightarrow \text{2RCOONa + H}_2$$

**Hydrolyse the lactone with warm dilute acid**

Warm dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ hydrolyses esters. The ring $\text{-COO-}$ opens with water to give a hydroxy-acid.
$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$
So this step creates 1 carboxylic acid $\text{-COOH}$ (1 reactive H) and 1 alcohol $\text{-OH}$ (1 reactive H). That is 2 so far.

**Dihydroxylate the alkenes with cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$**

Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ does mild syn addition to $\text{C=C}$, not oxidative cleavage. Each $\text{C=C}$ gives a diol.
$$\text{C=C + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HO-C-C-OH}$$
Santonin has 2 $\text{C=C}$ bonds, so we get $2 \times 2 = 4$ new alcohol $\text{-OH}$ groups. The ketone is unchanged under these mild conditions.

**Count all Na-reactive hydrogens in Q**

Add them together. From hydrolysis: 1 from $\text{-COOH}$ + 1 from $\text{-OH}$ = 2. From oxidation: 4 from two diols = 4.
$$\text{Total = 2 + 4 = 6 reactive H atoms}$$
So each molecule of Q has 6 hydrogen atoms that will liberate $\text{H}_2$ with Na.

options.A: 2 counts only the hydrolysis products (one $\text{-COOH}$ and one $\text{-OH}$). It forgets that cold $\text{KMnO}_4$ adds four more $\text{-OH}$ groups across the two $\text{C=C}$ bonds, all of which also react with Na.
options.B: 4 counts only the four $\text{-OH}$ groups from dihydroxylation of the two alkenes. It forgets the two $\text{O-H}$ protons created when the lactone ester is hydrolysed to a hydroxy-acid.
options.C: 5 comes from missing one group, often by thinking there is only one $\text{C=C}$ bond or by miscounting the lactone hydrolysis as giving only the carboxylic acid. In fact there are two $\text{C=C}$ bonds giving 4 $\text{-OH}$, plus 2 from hydrolysis.
options.D: 6 is correct: 1 $\text{-COOH}$ H + 1 alcohol H from lactone hydrolysis + 4 alcohol H from dihydroxylation of two $\text{C=C}$ bonds with cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$. All six are $\text{O-H}$ protons and react with sodium to give $\text{H}_2$.
